description: How mobile networks are built and run end to end: cellular concepts and spectrum, the GSM, UMTS, LTE and 5G architectures and their protocols, mobility management and roaming, and the SMS, USSD and data services that carry mobile money and everyday traffic. Every procedure, from attach and handover to a USSD session, is traced message by message in a network simulator, and a network is planned for real coverage and traffic targets.
modelledOn: 3GPP Technical Specifications for GSM, UMTS, LTE and 5G NR
Sauter, From GSM to LTE-Advanced Pro and 5G: An Introduction to Mobile Networks and Mobile Broadband
Holma and Toskala, LTE for UMTS: Evolution to LTE-Advanced
Dahlman, Parkvall and Skold, 5G NR: The Next Generation Wireless Access Technology
outcomes: Explain the cellular concept and plan cells, frequency reuse and capacity for a given coverage area and traffic load.
Describe the radio access and core networks of GSM, UMTS, LTE and 5G and the role of each network element and interface.
Trace signalling procedures such as attach, authentication, bearer setup, paging and handover across the protocol stack.
Analyse mobility management, location updating and roaming and their cost in signalling load and latency.
Design SMS, USSD and mobile data services and explain how the operator's network delivers and charges for them.
Compare 4G and 5G deployment options and assess them for urban and rural coverage in Ghana and the wider region.

units.title: Cellular concepts and the evolution of mobile networks
topics: Generations of mobile networks from 1G analogue to 5G: what each added in services, data rate and architecture; the roles of 3GPP and the ITU
Cells, clusters and frequency reuse; reuse distance, co-channel interference and the signal-to-interference ratio
Capacity: cell splitting, sectoring, microcells, picocells and small cells; traffic in Erlangs and grade of service
Macro, micro and umbrella cell layers; coverage-limited versus capacity-limited cells
Mobile markets in Africa: operator landscape, tower sharing, mobile penetration and the rural coverage gap

units.title: Radio access and spectrum
topics: Spectrum bands for 2G to 5G (sub-1 GHz, mid-band, millimetre wave); the coverage and capacity trade-offs of each
Spectrum licensing and auctions; the National Communications Authority and spectrum policy in Ghana
Duplexing (FDD, TDD) and multiple access (FDMA, TDMA, CDMA, OFDMA) as used by each generation
Link budget and cell range; why low bands matter for rural cell coverage
Base station hardware: antennas, remote radio heads, baseband units; backhaul over microwave, fibre and satellite

units.title: GSM architecture and protocols
topics: GSM network elements: MS, SIM, BTS, BSC, MSC, HLR, VLR, AuC, EIR; the Um, Abis and A interfaces
Air interface: TDMA frames, timeslots, logical channels (traffic, broadcast, common and dedicated control)
Signalling: SS7, MAP and the GSM protocol stack (LAPDm, RR, MM, CM)
Call setup for mobile-originated and mobile-terminated calls; paging and channel assignment
Security: IMSI and TMSI, A3 and A8 challenge-response authentication, A5 ciphering and the known weaknesses of 2G

units.title: GPRS and 3G UMTS
topics: GPRS and EDGE: packet data over GSM, SGSN and GGSN, PDP contexts, the Gn and Gi interfaces
UMTS architecture: UTRAN with NodeB and RNC, the Iub and Iu interfaces, circuit-switched and packet-switched domains
WCDMA radio: spreading, fast power control, soft handover and the near-far problem
HSPA and HSPA+: higher data rates, fast scheduling and the shift to data-dominated traffic
Mutual authentication with AKA and the improvements over GSM security

units.title: 4G LTE: E-UTRAN and the Evolved Packet Core
topics: Flat all-IP architecture: eNodeB, MME, S-GW, P-GW, HSS, PCRF; the S1, X2 and S11 interfaces
LTE radio: OFDMA downlink, SC-FDMA uplink, resource blocks, frame structure, MIMO and carrier aggregation
Protocol stack: PDCP, RLC, MAC and PHY in the user plane; RRC and NAS in the control plane
Attach, default and dedicated bearers, QoS class identifiers and policy control
Voice over LTE with IMS; circuit-switched fallback as a transition
Simulating an LTE attach and measuring control-plane latency

units.title: Mobility management and roaming
topics: Idle-mode mobility: location, routing and tracking areas; the trade-off between location updating and paging
Connected-mode handover: measurement reports, hard, soft and X2-based handover, inter-RAT handover
Handover failures, ping-pong and parameter tuning (hysteresis, time to trigger)
National and international roaming: home routing versus local breakout, HLR and VLR signalling, GRX and IPX
Cross-border roaming arrangements in East and West Africa and their effect on what subscribers pay

units.title: 5G networks
topics: 5G use cases: enhanced mobile broadband, massive machine-type communication, ultra-reliable low-latency communication
5G NR radio: flexible numerology, bandwidth parts, massive MIMO and beamforming, millimetre wave
5G core service-based architecture: AMF, SMF, UPF, AUSF, UDM, PCF, NRF; HTTP-based service interfaces
Non-standalone and standalone deployment options; dual connectivity with LTE
Network slicing, multi-access edge computing and the virtualised, cloud-native core
Fixed wireless access and the business case for 5G in African cities versus extending 4G to rural areas

units.title: Mobile data services, SMS and USSD
topics: SMS: the SMSC, store and forward, MAP signalling, delivery reports, SMS over IMS and bulk SMS gateways
USSD: session-oriented signalling, mobile-initiated and network-initiated sessions, the USSD gateway and session timeouts
Designing USSD menus for mobile money and government services: shortcodes such as *170#, menu depth and session limits
Mobile data services: APNs, DNS, carrier-grade NAT, data bundles and charging (online and offline charging, the OCS)
Security and fraud in mobile services: SIM swap, SS7 attacks, SMS one-time passwords and their weaknesses

units.title: Network planning, operations and capstone
topics: Radio network planning: coverage prediction, capacity dimensioning, site selection and drive tests
Key performance indicators: call setup success, drop rate, handover success, throughput; network optimisation
Network management with OSS and BSS; powering off-grid sites with solar and generators
Capstone: plan an LTE network for a rural Ghanaian district and simulate attach, handover and a USSD transaction across it

schedule.title: Generations, cells and frequency reuse
schedule.exercise: Problem set: compute the reuse distance and the signal-to-interference ratio for cluster sizes 3, 4, 7 and 12, and traffic in Erlangs for a cell with given call rates.

tasks.title: Compute reuse distance and signal-to-interference ratio for cluster sizes 3, 4, 7 and 12 and tabulate them
Use the Erlang B formula to find the channels needed for 20 Erlangs at 2 percent blocking, and plot blocking against channel count
Plan cell splitting and sectoring for a congested city cell by comparing capacity gain and interference in a simulated cellular layout

schedule.title: Cell layers and the African mobile market
schedule.exercise: Short report: describe how tower sharing and low-band spectrum could extend coverage to villages in one Ghanaian district, with a simple cost comparison.

tasks.title: Place macro, micro and small cells on a simulated map and mark which areas are coverage-limited and which are capacity-limited
Configure three cell layers over one town and test whether a fast-moving user is served by the macro layer to avoid repeated handovers
Estimate the break-even population for a rural tower from build and operating costs and revenue per user, then test the effect of tower sharing

schedule.title: Spectrum, multiple access and link budgets
schedule.exercise: Compare 900 MHz, 1800 MHz, 3.5 GHz and 26 GHz in a table of range, capacity and building penetration, and state which suit rural and urban Ghana.

tasks.title: Match each of GSM, UMTS, LTE and 5G to its duplexing and multiple-access scheme, and compute the resource slots of a TDMA frame
Compute a link budget and the cell range at 900 MHz and 2100 MHz for given power, antenna gain and receiver sensitivity
Compare coverage and capacity for 700 MHz and 3.5 GHz deployments of the same rural site using the wireless link simulator and report the findings

schedule.title: GSM architecture, air interface and signalling
schedule.exercise: Label a GSM network diagram with all elements and interfaces, then write the sequence of messages for a location update.

tasks.title: Build a GSM network diagram in the simulator with MS, BTS, BSC, MSC and registers, and label the Um, Abis and A interfaces
Decode a TDMA frame in the simulator, assign eight mobile stations to timeslots, and identify the broadcast and dedicated control channels
Trace the GSM protocol stack and signalling messages for a location update, and find which message is missing in a faulty capture

schedule.title: Call setup and 2G security
schedule.exercise: Explain in writing the A3, A8 and A5 steps of a challenge-response authentication, and list two weaknesses of 2G that later generations fixed.

tasks.title: Trace the message flow of a mobile-originated call from channel request to alerting, and fill in the table of signalling messages
Trace a mobile-terminated call through paging and channel assignment, and find the point where a given trace fails to reach the called phone
Simulate a GSM challenge-response authentication with a fake base station, show what an attacker can learn, and recommend countermeasures

schedule.title: GPRS, UMTS and HSPA
schedule.exercise: Compare the 2G packet core (SGSN, GGSN) with the 3G core, mapping each element, interface and domain, and note why handover is soft in WCDMA.

tasks.title: Establish a PDP context on a simulated GPRS network and trace the IP address given by the GGSN to the mobile
Simulate WCDMA spreading and despreading with two users and show how a near user's signal interferes with a far user's without power control
Compare voice and data load on a simulated UMTS cell as HSPA users grow, and find the user count at which downlink throughput per user falls below 1 Mbps

schedule.title: LTE architecture and radio
schedule.exercise: Draw the LTE architecture with all interfaces, then explain how OFDMA resource blocks are assigned to three users with different channel quality.

tasks.title: Build an LTE network in the simulator with an eNodeB, MME, S-GW and P-GW, and label the S1, X2 and S11 interfaces
Compute the resource blocks and peak throughput of a 20 MHz LTE carrier with 2 by 2 MIMO and compare it with a 5 MHz carrier
Trace the user-plane and control-plane protocol stacks for a data session and identify which layer causes a packet loss in a faulty trace

schedule.title: LTE bearers, voice and attach
schedule.exercise: Write the ordered steps of an LTE attach and default bearer setup, naming the message and the network element for each step.

tasks.title: Attach a mobile to a simulated LTE network and identify the default bearer and its IP address in the session table
Add a dedicated bearer with a guaranteed bit rate for voice over LTE, and verify that voice keeps its quality when data load rises
Measure control-plane latency of an LTE attach in the simulator under three radio conditions, and find which step dominates the delay

schedule.title: Mobility, handover and roaming
schedule.exercise: Problem set: given a measurement report sequence, decide when a handover triggers with hysteresis and time-to-trigger, and spot a ping-pong.

tasks.title: Compare location-update traffic and paging load for tracking areas of 5, 20 and 50 cells, and choose the best balance
Move a mobile between two cells in the simulator and observe the measurement reports and handover decision with given parameters
Tune hysteresis and time-to-trigger to remove ping-pong handovers on a highway scenario without increasing call drops, and report the final setting

schedule.title: 5G radio, core and deployment
schedule.exercise: Compare 5G standalone and non-standalone options in a table of core, radio, cost and latency, and recommend one for an African city rollout.

tasks.title: Match twelve services to eMBB, mMTC and URLLC and plot the latency and data rate each needs
Compute the beamforming gain and beam width of massive MIMO arrays of 8, 32 and 64 elements, and compare coverage at 3.5 GHz and 26 GHz
Build a 5G service-based core with AMF, SMF and UPF, create video and low-latency control slices, and show each keeps its guarantee under congestion

schedule.title: 5G business cases and fixed wireless access
schedule.exercise: Write a short business case: should an operator deploy 5G in Accra, extend 4G to rural villages, or both? Give the cost, revenue and coverage assumptions.

tasks.title: Compare non-standalone and standalone 5G connections in the simulator and record the core network and radio used in each
Compute the cost per covered person for 5G in a dense city and 4G in a rural district, and compare the two figures
Evaluate a fixed wireless access offer for homes by modelling subscriber revenue, equipment cost and capacity, and find the number of subscribers per site that breaks even

schedule.title: SMS, USSD and mobile data services
schedule.exercise: Design a USSD menu and session flow for paying a utility bill with mobile money, including timeouts, shortcodes and a failure path, and test it with five scenarios.

tasks.title: Walk a USSD session for a balance check through the gateway in the simulator and note each request and response
Design a USSD menu of at most four levels for a mobile money transfer and test it against session timeout and wrong-input cases
Investigate a SIM swap fraud case in a branching scenario, gathering evidence from SMS and network logs and choosing containment steps for the operator

schedule.title: Network planning, operations and capstone
schedule.exercise: Capstone report: dimension an LTE network for a rural district with site locations, a backhaul choice, a solar power plan and the expected KPI targets.

tasks.title: Compute call setup success rate, drop rate and handover success rate from a table of counters and flag KPIs below target
Place sites to cover a rural district map in the simulator and check the coverage prediction against the required service levels
Plan an LTE network for a rural district and simulate an attach, a handover and a USSD mobile money transaction across it, and report KPIs
